subject: environmental-science
title: Salinisation and Desertification
welcome_lead: Irrigation gone wrong, drylands stressed — global land in crisis.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on salinisation, desertification and remediation.
final_note: Drylands are 41% of land area and house 38% of humanity — desertification is a human story.

walkthroughs.body_html: Irrigation raises water tables; evaporation concentrates salts at the surface. Affects 20% of global irrigated land.
UNCCD estimates 12 Mha lost annually. Drivers: overgrazing, deforestation, climate variability.
Excess water leaches salts; gypsum displaces Na⁺ in sodic soils. Re-vegetation and conservation tillage rebuild soil structure.

mcqs.q: What is the leading driver of global deforestation?
options: Forest fires alone.
Bacteria produce them.
Agriculture (especially cattle ranching, soy, palm oil).
Logging for timber and paper.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
Forest fires alone.
Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: Bacteria produce them.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
